option_relations.rationale: SARS-CoV-2-associated optic neuritis is a broader category that includes post-infectious optic neuritis, as the virus can cause inflammation leading to optic neuritis.

Immune-mediated parainfectious optic neuritis is clinically equivalent to post-infectious optic neuritis, as both describe optic nerve inflammation occurring after an infection due to an immune response.
COVID-19-associated optic neuritis and retinal vasculitis is a broader diagnosis that includes optic neuritis, and given the context of COVID-19, it can encompass a post-infectious etiology.

Inflammation-induced ocular neuropathy associated with SARS-CoV-2-induced panuveitis is a broader and more complex diagnosis that includes optic neuropathy (which optic neuritis is a form of) and is associated with SARS-CoV-2, thus encompassing a post-infectious optic neuritis.
